title: Retry a command several times with a growing wait between tries
summary: Runs a command again when it fails, waiting a little longer each time (2, 4, 8 seconds and so on), and stops with an error after the last allowed try.

steps.explain: Run a command that always fails, with one-second waits to keep the test short. You see each attempt, then the final message.

steps.explain: Create a command that fails twice and succeeds on the third try. It keeps its count in count.txt.
steps.cmd:
printf '#!/usr/bin/env bash
n=$(cat count.txt 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
n=$((n + 1))
echo "$n" > count.txt
(( n >= 3 ))
' > flaky.sh && chmod +x flaky.sh
steps.expect: No output. flaky.sh now exists and can be run.

steps.explain: Retry the flaky command. It succeeds on attempt 3, so the script exits with code 0.
steps.expect: success on attempt 3, then exit code 0

placeholders.name: MAX_TRIES
placeholders.description: How many times to try in total, at least 1

warnings: Retry only commands that are safe to repeat. A copy or a payment can happen twice if the first try actually worked but reported an error.
Always set a maximum number of tries. Without one, a permanent error repeats forever.
The command's output appears on every try, so a command that prints a lot fills the screen fast.

script.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# retry.sh - run a command up to MAX_TRIES times, waiting longer after each failure.
# Usage: ./retry.sh MAX_TRIES COMMAND [ARGS...]
# The first wait is BASE_DELAY seconds (environment variable, default 2).
# The wait doubles after every failure: 2s, 4s, 8s, ...
# Exit code: 0 when the command succeeded, otherwise the command's last exit code.

set -euo pipefail

BASE_DELAY=${BASE_DELAY:-2}

if (( $# < 2 )); then
    echo "usage: $0 MAX_TRIES COMMAND [ARGS...]" >&2
    exit 2
fi
MAX_TRIES=$1
shift

if ! [[ $MAX_TRIES =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]]; then
    echo "error: MAX_TRIES must be a whole number of 1 or more" >&2
    exit 2
fi

delay=$BASE_DELAY
attempt=1
while true; do
    # "status=0; cmd || status=$?" records the exit code without
    # letting set -e stop the script when the command fails.
    status=0
    "$@" || status=$?
    if (( status == 0 )); then
        echo "success on attempt $attempt" >&2
        exit 0
    fi
    if (( attempt >= MAX_TRIES )); then
        echo "giving up after $attempt attempts (last exit code $status)" >&2
        exit "$status"
    fi
    echo "attempt $attempt failed (exit code $status), retrying in ${delay}s" >&2
    sleep "$delay"
    delay=$((delay * 2))
    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
done

prerequisites: A Linux terminal with bash 4 or newer
